title: Torus centralizers under finite radicial isogenies
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and geometric connectedness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $G,G\prime$ be smooth and geometrically connected. A torus is a group becoming $\mathbf G_m^r$ over an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], where $r\geq0$ and $\mathbf G_m(R)=R^\times$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type, def-sc-gm-ga]. A maximal torus is maximal among closed torus subgroups [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. For a torus $T\subseteq J$, $C_J(T)$ is the closed subgroup representing the functor of elements commuting with $T$ after every commutative algebra extension, as in [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected]. Let $f:G\to G\prime$ be a finite faithfully flat radicial homomorphism: through $f^*:k[G\prime]\to k[G]$ the coordinate ring $k[G]$ is a finite faithfully flat $k[G\prime]$-module, and after every algebraically closed field extension $f$ is injective on points. Let $T\subseteq G$ and $T\prime\subseteq G\prime$ be tori such that $f$ restricts to a faithfully flat homomorphism $T\to T\prime$. Then $T$ is maximal in $G$ if and only if $T\prime$ is maximal in $G\prime$, and the restriction of $f$ induces a finite faithfully flat radicial homomorphism $C_G(T)\to C_{G\prime}(T\prime)$. Kernels need not be smooth or trivial. No assertion of surjectivity on $k$-rational points is made, and no perfectness or reductivity assumption is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated comparison supplying the omitted isogeny passage between Proposition 17.80 (p.378) and Theorem 17.91 (p.381). Maximality uses Proposition 17.20 (pp.357–358) and Theorem 17.82 (p.379); smooth connected torus centralizers are 17.72 (p.376). Faithfully flat scheme-theoretic images use Theorem 3.34 (p.75). This combined comparison is not stated verbatim in Milne.

proof.text: Put $F=\bar k$. Faithful flatness of $f_F$ and of $T_F\to T'_F$ follows by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change]; smoothness of the ambient groups follows by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). They are connected by the geometric-connectedness hypothesis. By [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension], maximality of either torus can be tested over $F$. The point criterion [lem-sfb-affine-group-homomorphism-image] makes $G(F)\to G'(F)$ surjective, and the radicial hypothesis makes it injective. Also $T(F)\to T'(F)$ is surjective: faithful flatness gives a prime over the ideal of any $F$-point by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]; choose a maximal ideal containing it. Its contraction is the original maximal ideal, and its residue field is $F$ by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing](1). Here and below an $F$-point of a group denotes a point of its scalar extension.

source.place: Agent comparison of Theorem 3.34 (p.75), Proposition 5.47 (p.110), Proposition 17.20 (pp.357–358), Theorem 17.82 (p.379), and torus centralizers (17.72, p.376).

proof.text: If $T_F$ is maximal, [lem-sfb-quotient-borel-torus-images] applied to $f_F$ says that its scheme-theoretic image is maximal. This image is $T'_F$: the given faithfully flat map to the closed subgroup $T'_F$ is an image factorization (its coordinate map is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective]). Conversely suppose $T'_F$ maximal. The same quotient theorem supplies a maximal torus $S\subseteq G_F$ whose image is $T'_F$, with $S\to T'_F$ faithfully flat. The prime-and-maximal-ideal argument in step 1 applies also to $S\to T'_F$, so both $S(F)\to T'(F)$ and $T(F)\to T'(F)$ are surjective. Injectivity of $f_F$ therefore gives $S(F)=T(F)$. Both $S$ and $T_F$ have reduced Laurent-polynomial coordinate algebras. For every equation cutting out either closed subgroup in $G_F$, its restriction to the other vanishes at every $F$-point, hence is zero by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing](2). Thus their defining ideals agree, $S=T_F$, so $T_F$ is maximal. Step 1 transfers both implications to $k$.

source.place: Agent comparison of Theorem 3.34 (p.75), Proposition 5.47 (p.110), Proposition 17.20 (pp.357–358), Theorem 17.82 (p.379), and torus centralizers (17.72, p.376).

proof.text: Write $C=C_G(T)$ and $D=C_{G'}(T')$. They are smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup schemes by [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected]. Construct $h:C\to D$ over $k$ as follows. For any $k$-algebra $A$ and $x\in C(A)$, the commutator morphism $T'_A\to G'_A$, $t'\mapsto f(x)t'f(x)^{-1}t'^{-1}$, becomes the constant identity after precomposition with $T_A\to T'_A$, since $x$ commutes with $T$ universally. The map $A[T']\to A[T]$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change], hence injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective]. Equality of the two pullbacks of every coordinate function therefore gives equality of the two morphisms on $T'_A$. This works after every further $A$-algebra extension, so $f(x)\in D(A)$. The construction is natural in $A$ and respects multiplication; the represented subgroup functors therefore give the asserted homomorphism $h$.

source.place: Agent comparison of Theorem 3.34 (p.75), Proposition 5.47 (p.110), Proposition 17.20 (pp.357–358), Theorem 17.82 (p.379), and torus centralizers (17.72, p.376).

proof.text: Centralizer formation here commutes with field extension directly from its functor: for an extension $K/k$ and a $K$-algebra $A$, the condition of commuting after every further $A$-algebra extension is the same whether $T$ is first extended to $K$ or not. Thus $C_F=C_{G_F}(T_F)$ and $D_F=C_{G'_F}(T'_F)$. Given $y\in D_F(F)$, step 1 supplies its unique lift $x\in G_F(F)$. For each $t\in T_F(F)$, $f_F(xtx^{-1}t^{-1})=1$, hence $xtx^{-1}t^{-1}=1$. The morphism $T_F\to G_F$, $t\mapsto xtx^{-1}t^{-1}$, is therefore the identity point on all $F$-points. Pull back each coordinate function and subtract its value at the identity. The resulting function on the reduced Laurent-polynomial algebra $F[T]$ vanishes at every $F$-point, hence is zero by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing](2). The commutator morphism is constant as a scheme morphism, also on nonreduced test algebras. Thus $x\in C_F(F)$ and $h_F$ is surjective on $F$-points.

source.place: Agent comparison of Theorem 3.34 (p.75), Proposition 5.47 (p.110), Proposition 17.20 (pp.357–358), Theorem 17.82 (p.379), and torus centralizers (17.72, p.376).

proof.text: The group $D_F$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected], applied over $F$. The point criterion [lem-sfb-affine-group-homomorphism-image] now makes $h_F:C_F\to D_F$ faithfully flat. To descend this assertion, put $A=k[D]$, $B=k[C]$, so $F\otimes_k B$ is faithfully flat over $F\otimes_k A$. For an injection $M\hookrightarrow N$ of $A$-modules, the kernel of $M\otimes_A B\to N\otimes_A B$ becomes zero after tensoring with $F$, since field extension is exact and $h_F$ is flat. A $k$-vector space whose tensor with $F$ is zero is zero (a basis stays linearly independent). Hence $B$ is flat over $A$. If $M\otimes_A B=0$, then faithful flatness upstairs gives $F\otimes_k M=0$, hence $M=0$. This proves faithful flatness over $k$, without any assertion on $k$-points.

source.place: Agent comparison of Theorem 3.34 (p.75), Proposition 5.47 (p.110), Proposition 17.20 (pp.357–358), Theorem 17.82 (p.379), and torus centralizers (17.72, p.376).

proof.text: Finiteness of the restriction is a direct coordinate-module calculation. Set $R=k[G']$ and $S=k[G]$; let $I\subset R$ and $J\subset S$ cut out $D$ and $C$. Step 3 says $f^*(I)\subset J$. Thus $h^*:R/I\to S/J$ is induced by $f^*$. If $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ generate the finite $R$-module $S$, their classes generate $S/J$ over $R/I$: reduce any expression $s=\sum_i r_i s_i$ modulo $J$ and $I$. Therefore $h$ is finite. For every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, equality of two elements of $C(\Omega)$ after applying $h$ implies their equality in $G(\Omega)$ by radicial injectivity of $f$, and hence equality in the closed subgroup $C$. This is exactly the radicial condition used in the statement. Together with step 5 this proves every asserted property of $h$; its kernel was never assumed smooth or trivial.

Step 1: every hypothesis of the field-extension node and of the point criterion holds over F=k̄; T(F)->T'(F) is surjective by the prime/maximal-ideal contraction argument plus Nullstellensatz clause (1). Step 2: the forward direction comes from quotient-borel-torus-images applied to f_F, and the image is T'_F because F[T']->F[T] is injective. For the converse, the lifted maximal torus S has the same F-points as T_F by radicial injectivity, and reduced Laurent coordinate rings plus Nullstellensatz clause (2) give S=T_F as schemes. Step 3: h is constructed on all test algebras, using faithfully flat ⇒ injective for A[T']->A[T]. Step 4: base change of centralizers follows directly from the definition by test algebras, and geometric surjectivity uses vanishing on the reduced F[T_F]. Step 5: the point criterion with smooth D_F, then an elementary descent of faithful flatness along F/k. Step 6: finiteness and radicial injectivity are elementary module checks. Edge cases checked: rank-zero torus, identity, Frobenius on G_m (kernel mu_p), imperfect k. The statement is unchanged and no target is weakened.
